summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted electively for IV diuresis and right heart catheterization due to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure and suspected constrictive physiology. During the hospitalization, she was diagnosed with a bacterial urinary tract infection treated with ciprofloxacin and ceftriaxone, and new-onset type 2 diabetes managed with insulin. She struggled with fluid compliance due to polydipsia, which hindered diuresis. After a right heart cath confirmed constrictive physiology likely related to obesity and HIV, plans were made for further imaging. However, the patient left against medical advice when her mother became critically ill, discontinuing treatment prematurely. She did not return as promised, and her PCP was notified.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Asymptomatic human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] infection status
Personal history of other infectious and parasitic diseases
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of ovary
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
Dermatitis due to drugs and medicines taken internally
Other drugs and medicinal substances causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
